newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine cardinal slams national ID card plan.
newsitem.headline: Philippine cardinal slams national ID card plan.

text.p: The Philippines' most influential churchman on Tuesday attacked President Fidel Ramos's national ID card system as an authoritarian abuse of power.
"It would be immoral to implement a national ID system without the informed and reflected consent of the citizenry," Cardinal Jaime Sin said, joining mounting opposition to the identity card system.
"Clearly this consent has not been attained."
Opposition politicians have said the system could be used to monitor political activities, and have warned that Ramos could face impeachment if he did not withdraw his order.
Ramos ordered the adoption of the computerised system whereby Filipinos would be issued cards that officials say would make it easier to transact business with the government and minimise fraud.
Sin said Ramos' order left many questions unanswered, such as who would have access to government data on individuals and how could such data be protected from abuse.

"Data abused is privacy invaded, or truth falsified," Sin said. "Such is the fodder of fraud, and the contrivance of usurpers of democratic power. A project pushed in the face of so many unanswered questions can only be sinister."
